title: If Only We Had Known: A Conversation About Regrets

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I've been thinking a lot lately. Do you ever look back and wish you'd made different choices?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: All the time, honestly. I sometimes wish I hadn't dropped out of the architecture programme. I really regret that decision.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I didn't know you had studied architecture. What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Life happened. My father got ill, I needed to work, and I thought — I'll come back to it. But I never did. If only I had found a way to do both. I know that sounds unrealistic, but…

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: No, it doesn't sound unrealistic. It sounds human. I have my own version of that story. I wish I had taken the job in London when it was offered. I turned it down because I was too scared.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Fear is the great regret-maker, isn't it? Supposing you had gone — do you think your life would look completely different?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Almost certainly. I'd probably be in a completely different field. Which is strange to imagine. But then again — what if I'd been miserable there? We only ever see one path.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: That's true. I often think: if I had stayed in the programme, maybe I would have graduated but never practised. Maybe I'd have hated it by now. We idealise the roads not taken.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Exactly. I think the honest version is: I wish I had been braver, not necessarily that I wish the outcome had been different. The courage is what I miss.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: That's a really interesting distinction. So it's not "if only I had gone to London" — it's "if only I had been the kind of person who could take that risk."

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Yes. And I think I am that person now. Which means the regret might actually have been useful. It pushed me to become braver over time.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: So what starts as regret can turn into growth. I hadn't thought of it that way. Maybe I should have thanked my past self for failing, rather than blaming him.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Should have thanked, could have thanked — but didn't! That's the grammar of life, I suppose. We always know what we should have done in hindsight.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Ha! Yes. In hindsight, everything is obvious. Imagine if we could always see that clearly in the moment. The world would be very different.
